confidence_notes: The food and drink anchors come from web searches I ran on aggregated sources: Numbeo (October 2026), Wise, world-prices.com, Exiap and TravelTables, plus nightlife guides. I converted dirham prices at about 9.2 to 10 MAD per USD. Restaurant meals and coffee have the strongest support. The sources agree: an inexpensive meal is about 35-50 MAD, a cappuccino about 13-18 MAD and a mid-range meal for two about 180-250 MAD. Beer is less certain. Numbeo's 50 MAD per pint seems high, while other sources put bottled beer at 17-20 MAD. Only a few licensed venues serve alcohol, so I estimated a restaurant draft at about 35-40 MAD. Cocktail and wine evidence is thin. Cocktails rest on guide estimates of about $5.40 in standard lounges and $9-11 at rooftop or upscale venues. The wine glass price is based on its relationship to beer and on retail bottle prices of 40-60 MAD. I raised prices slightly for July 2026, which is peak season. The accommodation anchors are general model estimates for the summer peak in a popular coastal medina town. I did not search for accommodation prices or check any live listings.
comparable_city_reasoning: I scaled restaurant prices from Essaouira's own cost-of-living data. For accommodation and alcohol, I compared Essaouira with Moroccan tourist towns like Chefchaouen and Taghazout, which have riad-style guesthouses and few licensed bars. Essaouira is usually somewhat cheaper than Marrakech. Rooms cost more in July because of summer demand from Moroccan and European visitors.
